summary: Hideomi Yaita specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral coursework at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa works in religious studies, having studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1997.
Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao.
Hideto Ono works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998), research student at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at Osaka Prefectural Kitano High School and the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). He held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1946).

Hideyo Ogawa works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He held faculty posts at Hiroshima University, serving as associate professor (~1989–1999) and as professor of Indian philosophy in the Graduate School of Letters (~1999–2020; attested 2026).

Hideyuki Matsumori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006), where he later served as assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Himanshu Prabha Ray is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Panjab University, Cambridge (~1971–1974), and JNU (~1974–1984). She was an associate professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and served as chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf studied linguistics and religious studies at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1807–1811). He held an academic appointment at the University of Breslau from circa 1813 until 1861.

Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia worked in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he held appointments as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as University Teacher for Ph.D. students in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward studied at Harvard (B.A. ~1958–1962) and Yale (M.A. 1966–1975). A scholar of art history and Buddhist studies, he taught at Michigan (1972–1982) and Vermont (~1982–1986), then served as Asian art curator at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri studied at DAV College Lahore and Oriental College. Working in Indology and archaeology, he held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India, several regional museums, and served as Baroda State's Director of Archaeology (1934–1942) and Government Epigraphist (attested 1931).

Hirofumi Isoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his doctorate at Tohoku University by 1966. He served at Tohoku University as lecturer (attested 1972) and associate professor (attested 1989–2000), and became professor emeritus at Shimane University (attested 1974).

Hirofumi Toda specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seiren Matsunami (~1958–1965). He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1978–2000) and was a special member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 1985).
Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. She held a post as senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and later held positions at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Hiromasa Tosaki, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, earned his PhD at Kyushu University and studied at Harvard. He served as professor at Kyushu University (~1978–1993) and held a post at Chikushi Jogakuen University (~1993–2000).

Hiromi Habata earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2014) and later joined the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2021).
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, including as full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and continuing through at least 2006.
